lessons.title: Switching Jobs Mid-Year Without Ending Up With Short TDS

body.text: Each employer calculates your TDS as if its salary were your only income for the year. Change jobs without telling the new one what the old one paid, and both can deduct too little while doing everything by the book.

children.text: Arjun, a UX designer, spent April to September 2026 at a Chennai agency earning ₹1,00,000 a month, then moved to a Bengaluru product company at ₹1,50,000 a month. His total salary for tax year 2026-27 was ₹15,00,000. Neither employer deducted a single rupee of TDS. When he sat down to file his return in July 2027, he owed ₹97,500, plus interest. Nobody had made a calculation error. The system simply had no way of seeing his whole year.

Recall from Lesson 1 that payroll projects your salary for the full year and applies slab rates, the standard deduction and the rebate to that projection. When you have two employers in one year, each one runs that exercise separately.

columns.label: Each employer, separately

Checks the rebate against its own salary alone

Allows one standard deduction in total
Tests the rebate against your combined income

body.title: Quick Check: Two Form 130s, One Return
body.question: Arjun receives two Form 130 certificates, and each shows a standard deduction of ₹75,000. How much standard deduction can he claim in his return?
options: ₹37,500 from each employer, pro-rated by months
body.explanation: The standard deduction under Section 19 (formerly 16) is a single allowance per person per tax year, no matter how many employers paid you. Both certificates show it only because each employer computed tax in isolation. In the return, the combined salary gets it once.

markDefs.definition: The employee's declaration to an employer, under Section 392 read with Rule 204, of salary from other employers, other income, house property loss and TDS or TCS already suffered. It replaces Forms 12B and 12BAA.

children.text: Section 392 lets you give your new employer details of salary paid and TDS deducted by a previous employer in the same tax year, so it can compute tax on your combined salary. Under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 this goes in
, which merges the old Form 12B (salary from a previous employer) with Form 12BAA (other income and TDS or TCS).

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Old Name
body.textWithBlank: Before 1 April 2026, employees reported salary from a previous employer in the same year to their new employer using Form ___.
body.explanation: Form 12B carried previous-employer salary details. From tax year 2026-27 it is merged with Form 12BAA into Form 122.

children.text: Had Arjun handed his Bengaluru employer a Form 122 in October showing ₹6,00,000 of salary and ₹0 of TDS from Chennai, payroll would have projected ₹15,00,000 for the year, allowed one standard deduction, and spread the full ₹97,500 across his six remaining months.

body.title: Where does that interest come from?

children.text: If your tax for the year after TDS is ₹10,000 or more, the law expects you to pay advance tax in instalments. Arjun's entire ₹97,500 went unpaid until he filed, so two kinds of simple interest at 1% a month apply, both calculated on amounts rounded down to the nearest ₹100.

cells: 1% a month on ₹97,500 for April to July 2027, 4 months

children.text: The course on advance tax covers these rules in detail. For a job switcher, the lesson is simpler: a Form 122 in October would have avoided every rupee of it.
When the Old Employer Already Deducted

Most job switchers do have some TDS from their first employer. Form 122 also carries that figure, so the new employer deducts only what is still due on the combined salary. It neither ignores your previous salary nor charges you again for tax already paid.

body.title: Try It: Credit for What the Old Employer Took
body.prompt: Priyanka earned ₹2,00,000 a month at a Mumbai bank from April to July 2026. The bank projected ₹24,00,000 for the year and deducted ₹24,375 a month, ₹97,500 in total. In August she joined a Pune fintech at ₹1,50,000 a month and submitted Form 122. Both employers use the new regime. What monthly TDS should the Pune employer deduct from August to March?
body.explanation: Combined salary is ₹8,00,000 + ₹12,00,000 = ₹20,00,000. Taxable income after one standard deduction is ₹19,25,000, and tax with cess is ₹1,92,400. The bank already deducted ₹97,500, leaving ₹94,900 to be spread over 8 months: about ₹11,863 a month. Without Form 122, Pune would have projected only ₹12,00,000, which falls within the rebate, deducted nothing, and left her with a ₹94,900 bill at filing time.

body.text: Tell both employers the same regime. Each applies whatever you intimated to it, and a mismatch makes the combined figures in Form 122 meaningless. If you have no business income, your final regime choice is still made when you file your return.

children.text: The Other Job-Switch Trap: Withdrawing Your EPF
Changing jobs is also when many people are tempted to cash out their provident fund. If you withdraw more than

before completing five years of continuous service, the EPFO deducts TDS at 10% under Section 392(7) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 192A), or at a higher rate without a valid PAN. And the TDS is only the start: much of a premature withdrawal also becomes taxable income for that year.

body.title: Scenario: Rohit's Bike Fund
body.scenario: Rohit, a support engineer in Noida, is leaving his employer after three years. His EPF balance is ₹2,40,000. His new job starts in two weeks, and he is thinking of withdrawing the whole amount to buy a motorbike.
body.prompt: What will a withdrawal cost him, and what is the better alternative?
body.modelAnswer: Because his service is under five years and the amount is above ₹50,000, the EPFO will deduct 10% TDS, ₹24,000, if his PAN is linked to his UAN. More importantly, a premature withdrawal loses its tax-free status: his employer's contributions and the interest on them become taxable, as do his own contributions if he claimed them as a deduction in the old regime. He would also restart the five-year clock and give up years of compounding. The better route is to transfer the balance to his new employer's account through the EPFO member portal using his UAN. A transfer is not a withdrawal, attracts no TDS, and his three years of service count towards the five-year requirement.

body.label: EPFO Member Portal
body.description: Log in with your UAN to check your PF passbook, confirm your PAN is linked, and request a transfer of your balance to your new employer.

body.title: Before and After You Change Jobs
steps: Before leaving, download your last payslip and ask HR for a statement of salary paid and TDS deducted so far this tax year
Within your first month at the new job, submit Form 122 with those figures to the new employer's payroll
Tell the new employer the same tax regime you used with the old one
Transfer your EPF using your UAN instead of withdrawing it
After the year ends, check that TDS from both employers appears under their TANs in Form 26AS and AIS
Collect Form 130 from both employers by 15 June 2027 and report the combined salary, with one standard deduction, in your return

cards.definition: Declaration to your employer of salary from other employers, other income, house property loss and TDS or TCS already suffered. Replaces Forms 12B and 12BAA.
TDS lower than the tax actually due on your total income, commonly caused by two employers each computing tax in isolation.
TDS at 10% on EPF withdrawals above ₹50,000 before five years of continuous service. Formerly Section 192A.
Interest at 1% a month for not paying or underpaying advance tax. Formerly Section 234B.
Interest at 1% a month for deferring advance tax instalments. Formerly Section 234C.
Universal Account Number. Your single EPF identity across employers, used to transfer your balance when you change jobs.

points: Each employer computes salary TDS as if its salary were your only income, so two employers in one year can both under-deduct
Your return adds both salaries, allows one standard deduction and tests the rebate against combined income
Give your new employer Form 122 (replacing Forms 12B and 12BAA) with the previous employer's salary and TDS so it can deduct correctly
A shortfall of ₹10,000 or more can attract interest under Sections 424 and 425 (formerly 234B and 234C) on top of the tax
Form 122 also reports TDS the old employer already deducted, so the new employer recovers only the balance still due
Transfer your EPF when switching. Withdrawing above ₹50,000 before five years triggers 10% TDS under Section 392(7) and makes much of the amount taxable

Interest figures are simplified illustrations. Provisions reflect the position understood at the time of writing and can change.
